formulations.label: Tablets 60 mg (modified-release, three times daily)
formulations.note: The UK 60 mg diltiazem tablet SmPC describes a modified-release tablet taken three times daily.

src.q: Each tablet contains 60 mg of the active substance diltiazem hydrochloride.
Modified release tablet
The usual dose is one tablet (60 mg) three times daily.

bnf.note: BNF/BNFC is only available in the UK; not accessed.

items.t: Prophylaxis and treatment of angina pectoris (60 mg tablet).

src.q: 4.1 Therapeutic indications Prophylaxis and treatment of Angina Pectoris

items.t: Other UK diltiazem products (once-daily prolonged-release capsules) are also licensed for mild to moderate hypertension.

src.q: VIAZEM XL is indicated for the management of stable angina pectoris and the treatment of mild to moderate hypertension.

restrictions.note: No prescribing restriction stated in the UK diltiazem 60 mg tablet SmPC.

items.t: Adults: 60 mg three times daily; may increase to 360 mg/day in divided doses. Up to 480 mg/day has been used (especially unstable angina).

src.q: The usual dose is one tablet (60 mg) three times daily.
If necessary, the divided dose may be increased to 360mg/day. Higher doses up to 480mg/day have been used with benefit in some patients especially in unstable angina.

items.t: Elderly and hepatic or renal impairment: start 60 mg twice daily; measure heart rate regularly and do not increase the dose if heart rate is below 50 beats per minute.

src.q: The recommended starting dose is one tablet (60 mg) twice daily. The heart rate should be measured regularly in these groups of patients and the dose should not be increased if the heart rate falls below 50 beats per minute.

items.t: Safety and efficacy not established; not recommended for children.

src.q: Safety and efficacy in children have not been established. Therefore, diltiazem is not recommended for use in children.

items.t: Hypersensitivity to diltiazem or excipients.

src.q: Hypersensitivity to diltiazem or to any of the excipients listed in section 6.1.

items.t: Sick sinus syndrome or second/third-degree AV block without a functioning pacemaker; severe bradycardia (below 50 beats per minute); left ventricular failure with pulmonary stasis.

src.q: Sick sinus syndrome, 2nd or 3rd degree AV block in patients without a functioning pacemaker. Severe bradycardia (less than 50 beats per minute). Left ventricular failure with pulmonary stasis.

items.t: Breastfeeding (lactation).

src.q: Left ventricular failure with pulmonary stasis. Lactation.

items.t: With dantrolene infusion, ivabradine, lomitapide or asunaprevir.

src.q: Concurrent use with dantrolene infusion (see section 4.5). Combination with ivabradine (see section 4.5). Concurrent use with lomitapide (see section 4.5). Concurrent use with asunaprevir (see section 4.5).

items.t: Close observation in reduced left ventricular function, bradycardia, first-degree AV block or prolonged PR interval (risk of complete block). Monitor closely, especially heart rate, at the start.

src.q: Close observation is necessary in patients with reduced left ventricular function, bradycardia (risk of exacerbation) or with a 1st degree AV block or prolonged PR interval detected on the electrocardiogram
close monitoring, particularly of heart rate, should be carried out at the beginning of treatment.

items.t: Elderly, renal or hepatic insufficiency: plasma levels may rise.

src.q: Increase of plasma concentrations of diltiazem may be observed in the elderly and patients with renal or hepatic insufficiency.

items.t: Acute renal failure has been reported in cardiac patients (reduced LV function, severe bradycardia or severe hypotension); monitor renal function carefully.

src.q: Cases of acute renal failure secondary to decreased renal perfusion have been reported in patients with cardiac disease
Carefully monitoring renal function is advised.

items.t: Bronchospasm, including asthma aggravation, especially with bronchial hyper-reactivity; monitor respiratory function.

src.q: The use of diltiazem may induce bronchospasm, including asthma aggravation, especially in patients with preexisting bronchial hyper-reactivity.
Patients should be monitored for signs and symptoms of respiratory impairment during diltiazem therapy.

items.t: Diabetes (latent or manifest): monitor carefully (blood glucose may rise). Intestinal obstruction risk: use with caution. Mood changes including depression: consider stopping.

src.q: Careful monitoring is necessary in patients with latent or manifest diabetes mellitus due to a possible increase in blood glucose.
it should be used with caution in patients at risk of developing an intestinal obstruction.
In such cases, drug discontinuation should be considered.

items.t: General anaesthesia: inform the anaesthetist (additive cardiac depression).

src.q: In the case of general anaesthesia, the anaesthetist must be informed that the patient is taking diltiazem.

items.t: Galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption: should not take (contains lactose).

src.q: Patients with rare hereditary problems of galactose intolerance, the Lapp lactase deficiency, or glucose-galactose malabsorption should not take this medicine.

items.t: Beta-blockers: risk of rhythm disturbances (marked bradycardia, sinus arrest), SA/AV conduction problems and heart failure; use only with close clinical and ECG monitoring, especially at the start. Increased risk of depression reported.

src.q: Possibility of rhythm disturbances (pronounced bradycardia, sinus arrest), sino-atrial and atrio-ventricular conduction disturbances and heart failure (synergistic effect).
Such a combination must only be used under close clinical and ECG monitoring, particularly at the beginning of treatment.

items.t: Statins metabolised by CYP3A4 (simvastatin, atorvastatin): more myopathy/rhabdomyolysis risk; statin dose may need adjusting; prefer a non-CYP3A4 statin where possible. MHRA: maximum simvastatin 20 mg daily with diltiazem.

src.q: The risk of myopathy and rhabdomyolysis is increased by concomitant administration of diltiazem with statins metabolised by CYP3A4 (e.g. atorvastatin, fluvastatin, and simvastatin).
An adjustment of the dose of statin may be necessary
The maximum recommended dose of simvastatin co-administered with amlodipine or diltiazem is now 20 mg per day.

items.t: Alpha-blockers: may cause or worsen hypotension; combine only with strict blood pressure monitoring.

src.q: The combination of diltiazem with an alpha antagonist should be considered only with strict monitoring of blood pressure.

items.t: Nitrates: additive vasodilatation (hypotension, faintness); increase nitrate doses gradually.

src.q: Increased hypotensive effects and faintness (additive vasodilating effects).
the prescription of nitrate derivatives should only be carried out at gradually increasing doses.

items.t: Carbamazepine: levels rise; measure carbamazepine levels and adjust dose if needed.

src.q: Increase in circulating carbamazepine levels. It is recommended that the plasma carbamazepine concentrations be assayed and that the dose should be adjusted if necessary.

items.t: QT-prolonging medicines: diltiazem may prolong QT; combine only after careful risk-benefit assessment.

src.q: Diltiazem may lead to QT prolongation, when administered with drugs with potential/ known for prolonging the QT interval.
must be based on a careful assessment of the potential risks and benefits of the treatment.

items.t: Antiplatelet drugs: possible additive effect (diltiazem inhibits platelet aggregation).

src.q: potential additive effects when used with antiplatelet drugs should be considered.

items.t: Other: ciclosporin (reduce dose, monitor levels and renal function); phenytoin and theophylline levels rise; cimetidine raises diltiazem; rifampicin lowers it; lithium neurotoxicity; colchicine not recommended; DOACs (bleeding); midazolam/triazolam and methylprednisolone levels rise; amiodarone/digoxin more bradycardia; other antiarrhythmics not recommended; grapefruit juice raises exposure.

src.q: It is recommended that the ciclosporin dose be reduced, renal function be monitored
its concomitant prescription with other antiarrhythmic agents is not recommended
Grapefruit juice should be avoided if an interaction is suspected.

items.t: Renal impairment: plasma levels may rise; start 60 mg twice daily, check heart rate regularly, do not increase if below 50 beats per minute. Monitor renal function in cardiac patients.

src.q: Elderly and patients with impaired hepatic or renal function The recommended starting dose is one tablet (60 mg) twice daily.
Carefully monitoring renal function is advised.

items.t: Hepatic impairment: plasma levels may rise; start 60 mg twice daily, check heart rate regularly, do not increase if below 50 beats per minute.

src.q: Elderly and patients with impaired hepatic or renal function The recommended starting dose is one tablet (60 mg) twice daily.

items.t: SmPC: not recommended in pregnancy or in women of child-bearing potential not using effective contraception (reproductive toxicity in animals).

src.q: Diltiazem is therefore not recommended during pregnancy, as well as in women of child-bearing potential not using effective contraception.

items.t: BUMPS (calcium-channel blockers): no clear risks; calcium-channel blockers other than nifedipine are recommended only when benefits outweigh possible risks.

src.q: There are no clear risks of taking a calcium channel blocker in pregnancy.

The other calcium channel blockers are less commonly used, and while not thought to cause problems, will only be recommended if the benefits of treating a potentially serious or lifestyle-impacting condition outweigh any possible risks.

items.t: SmPC: excreted in breast milk; breastfeeding while taking diltiazem is contraindicated.

src.q: As this drug is excreted in breast milk, breast feeding whilst taking diltiazem is contraindicated.

items.t: SPS (differs from the SmPC): negligible amounts in milk; can be used with caution, but verapamil is preferred if a rate-limiting calcium-channel blocker is needed; monitor the infant for hypotension.

src.q: Diltiazem is excreted into breast milk in negligible amounts. It can be used with caution during breastfeeding, but if a rate-limiting calcium-channel blocker is required, verapamil is preferred.

items.t: Not recommended in women of child-bearing potential not using effective contraception.

src.q: as well as in women of child-bearing potential not using effective contraception.

items.t: Dizziness and malaise are common. The SmPC table also lists headache, flushing, AV block, palpitations, constipation, dyspepsia, gastric pain, nausea and peripheral oedema (frequency columns not readable in the page text).

src.q: dizziness (common), malaise (common)
Headache, dizziness
Constipation, dyspepsia, gastric pain, nausea
Peripheral oedema Malaise

items.t: Sinoatrial block, congestive heart failure, sinus arrest, cardiac arrest (asystole); bronchospasm; hepatitis; severe skin reactions (erythema multiforme including Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis, AGEP, exfoliative dermatitis); angioedema.

src.q: Sinoatrial block, congestive heart failure, sinus arrest, cardiac arrest (asystole)
erythema multiforme (including Steven-Johnson's syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis), sweating, exfoliative dermatitis, acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis

items.t: Overdose: marked hypotension with collapse and acute kidney injury, bradycardia, AV block, cardiac arrest; non-cardiogenic pulmonary oedema may appear 24-48 hours later.

src.q: pronounced hypotension leading to collapse and acute kidney injury
Non-cardiogenic pulmonary oedema has rarely been reported as a consequence of diltiazem overdose that may manifest with a delayed onset (24-48 hours post-ingestion)

items.t: Heart rate at the start of treatment (and regularly in elderly, renal or hepatic impairment).

src.q: close monitoring, particularly of heart rate, should be carried out at the beginning of treatment.
The heart rate should be measured regularly in these groups of patients

items.t: Renal function in cardiac patients; blood glucose in diabetes; respiratory symptoms.

src.q: Carefully monitoring renal function is advised.

src.q: Such a combination must only be used under close clinical and ECG monitoring, particularly at the beginning of treatment.

items.t: Mood changes or depression: consider stopping.

src.q: In such cases, drug discontinuation should be considered.

administration.note: No food or swallowing instructions stated in the UK diltiazem 60 mg tablet SmPC beyond the three-times-daily schedule.

items.t: Dizziness and malaise are common and may affect driving.

src.q: dizziness (common), malaise (common), the ability to drive and use machines could be altered.

items.t: Report low mood or depression.

src.q: Treatment with diltiazem may be associated with mood changes, including depression

items.t: Avoid grapefruit juice if an interaction is suspected.

src.q: Grapefruit juice should be avoided if an interaction is suspected.
